articleTitle: Enhanced Cooling Strategy for Electric Vehicle Drive Motors: An Approach to Liquid Cooling Pipe Structure Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Effectively designing the heat dissipation method and mode for an electric vehicle's drive motor is crucial for its stability, safety, and overall performance. This project aims to optimize the liquid cooling system in electric vehicle drive motors to address their low heat dissipation efficiency. This paper examines the heat dissipation performance of air-cooled and liquid-cooled models based on available data, and evaluates the heat dissipation mechanism of the drive motor. The structure of the permanent magnet synchronous motor's liquid cooling waterway was optimized using FLUENT software to ameliorate both flow rate and wall pressure. The optimal cooling performance was achieved by simulating and analyzing the temperature and other data, revealing that altering the pipe diameter width was effective. By enhancing motor cooling in this project, electric vehicle manufacturers will gain significant theoretical and practical advantages.

articleTitle: A Multi-Stage Planning Method for Coordinating Energy Storage and Transmission Network Considering the Flexibility of Line Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Renewable energy sources exhibit significant volatility and uncertainty, and their large-scale integration into the grid exacerbates the flexibility issues of the power system. This is primarily due to the insufficient supply of flexible resources and the limitations on line power transmission. Furthermore, there is currently limited research on the flexibility of line transmission. To address this, a multi-stage planning method for coordinating energy storage and transmission network considering the flexibility of line transmission is proposed. Initially, the line flexibility load rate is defined to evaluate the flexibility of line transmission. This flexibility is then incorporated into the constraints, and the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) theory is applied to measure the operational risk of excessive line flexibility load rates. Consequently, a comprehensive bi-level, multi-stage planning model is established, taking into account both investment costs and operational costs. Validation through an actual system in a province in Northwest China demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively enhance the economic and flexible operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Electromagnetic and Thermal Performances Between Consequent-Pole PM and Conventional SPM Motors for eVTOL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of conventional Surface Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (SPMSMs) and Consequent-Pole Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (CPPMSMs). The CPPMSM design retains only the N-pole permanent magnets, replacing the S-pole magnets with silicon steel sheets in a consequent-pole structure. This approach aims to reduce the use of permanent magnets and lower overall manufacturing costs. The study focuses on the electromagnetic performance and thermal dissipation of CPPMSMs compared to conventional PMSMs. Finite element simulation results show that the consequent-pole can reduce the amount of permanent magnets by 25.5% with the same torque output, while there is no significant increase in loss and temperature rise, thus confirming the superior performance of the CPPMSM. This motor has promising applications in electric Vertical Take-off and Landing(eVTOL), where reducing the number of permanent magnets, lowering losses, and managing temperature rise are critical.

articleTitle: Modelling of Line Outage Probability and Grid Risk Assessment Taking into Account Stochastic Load Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Under the vision of peak carbon and carbon neutral goals, the new power system mainly based on new energy poses new challenges to the safe operation of the power grid. Due to the influence of stochastic factors, which makes the complexity of grid structure and operational uncertainty increasing, the risk of large-scale power outages further increases, and the accurate assessment of the risk of power outage losses plays a significant role in the safe operation of power grids. This paper proposes a method to calculate stochastic load flow based on adaptive kernel density estimation and applies it to the self-organized critical model of the power grid, and finally selects value-at-risk (VaR) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) as the risk metrics for risk assessment of different line faults, so as to derive the weak links of the power grid. On this basis, the rationality of the proposed model is verified by simulating the IEEE39 nodes.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability Analysis of High Inertia Energy Storage Synchronous Condensers with the Impact of Different Reactive Power Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The high inertia energy storage synchronous condenser (HIESS) has emerged as a promising equipment in power electronic dominated power system due to its inherent capabilities of fast voltage regulation and frequency support. However, the control dynamics of HIESS are extremely sensitive to voltage disturbances, which makes HIESS easily affected by its various reactive power control (RPC) and become unstable under weak grid conditions. This paper first establishes a small-signal model of HIESS considering various RPC behavior and the dynamics of the phase-locked loop (PLL), simultaneously. Furthermore, the compact HIESS model has been developed which uses the single-input single-output (SISO) form to intuitively present the interaction between PLL and RPC under weak grid conditions. On this basis, the SISO system stability criteria can be used to assess the system stability performance intuitively. In this manner, the effects of different RPC methods, grid strength, reactive power reference, and PLL bandwidth on system stability performance are analyzed in detail. It reveals that the HIESS is more unstable when outputting capacitive reactive power under weak grid conditions. The high PLL bandwidth and type of CRPC can stabilize the system. Simulation results validate the correctness of the stability analysis.

Author Keywords: High inertia energy storage synchronous condensers (HIESS)

articleTitle: Research on Fault Early Warning of Mine High-Voltage Explosion-Proof Switch Based on Multivariate State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that most of the fault warnings of high-voltage explosion-proof switches in mines only set thresholds for single variables, a fault early warning model based on Multivariate State Estimation (MSET) was proposed, which used the similarity threshold to determine whether there was a fault and the cumulative error contribution rate to trace the fault point. Firstly, the modeling variables were selected, the data preprocessing was carried out, the historical memory matrix was constructed, and the effectiveness of the MSET model was verified. Then, the sliding window method is used to reduce noise interference, and the similarity function is used as the fault warning criterion, and the cumulative error contribution rate can be traced back to the fault point. Finally, the historical data of 10kV high-voltage explosion-proof switch in a coal mine was used as the test set for verification. The results show that this method can detect the abnormality of the underground explosion-proof switch in time, realize the early warning of the high-voltage explosion-proof switch, and has high accuracy and anti-interference ability.

articleTitle: Quantifying Cost of BESS for Providing Power System Regulation Service Considering Capacity Regeneration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Predicting capacity loss is the premise for battery energy storage system (BESS) owner to evaluate the marginal cost of providing auxiliary service and also the key to enhance the market competitiveness of BESS. Most existing studies are devoted to predicting capacity degradation with empirical models, ignoring the uncertainties during degradation such as the capacity regeneration phenomenon. This paper proposes an operation cost model that considering uncertain capacity degradation. By signal decomposition algorithm, the capacity curves are divided into trend, regeneration and random noise parts. The RBF neural network is used to predict the trend and regeneration parts. In contrast, the SVR model is employed to predict the random noise. On this basis, this paper utilizes the Maryland University dataset to train these data-driven models, which can reduce the RMSE from 4.25% To 1.56%. The regulation service market clearing simulation indicates that the proposed model enhances the profitability of BESS by an average of 6.78% and a maximum of 9.51%. This is attributed to accurately predict capacity loss and identify capacity regeneration phenomena.

articleTitle: BLDC Sideband Harmonic Suppression Based on Carrier Synchronization at Commutation Time
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: For the high-speed brushless direct current (BLDC) motor driven by square wave, especially for high-speed applications, sideband current harmonics will be produced due to the limited switching frequency of inverter and the limitation of low carrier-fundamental frequency ratio, resulting in additional torque ripples. Meanwhile, a higher switching frequency not only lead to more switching loss and harmonics, but also increase the cost. Therefore, this study mainly intend to improve the pulse width modulation (PWM) commutation technology through the carrier phase-shifting control. The sideband harmonic current component under the natural sampling mode was firstly analyzed, then an improved PWM modulation method-carrier synchronous commutation was proposed to reduce and control the current harmonic component, by periodically resetting the phase of the carrier at the commutation time to improve the utilization of the PWM pulse and reduce the sideband harmonics, so as to reduce the torque fluctuation. In the end, the simulation and experimental verification and comparison are also carried out to prove the suppression effect of carrier synchronous commutation on the current sideband harmonics and torque ripples.

articleTitle: Frequency-Constrained Economic Dispatch Considering Demand-Side Resource Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The integration of a high proportion of renewable energies into the power grid significantly reduces the inertia level of the power system and brings foreseeable frequency security risks. In order to deal with this problem, it is necessary to explore the regulation potential of flexible resources on the demand side and work with traditional frequency regulation units to ensure the frequency stability of the system. This paper proposes a frequency-constrained economic dispatch (FCED) model. First, considering that incorporating demand-side load resources into frequency regulation will significantly increase the complexity of frequency dynamics, different types of frequency response resources are modeled and aggregated. Then, the frequency dynamic process in different time intervals is depicted, and the frequency security constraints corresponding to each time interval are derived. Finally, the traditional security-constrained economic dispatch (SCED) is combined with frequency security constraints to obtain a novel FCED model. The results of the case studies based on the IEEE 30-Bus system show that the FCED model proposed in this paper can schedule load resources to maintain the frequency security of the system after contingencies occur and ensure the economic and stable operation of the system.

articleTitle: Safety Analysis and Research Based on Multi-Stage Game and Integrated Energy System Security Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this article, the safety problem in the integrated energy system is solved using the game theory method. Combined with the characteristics of integrated energy system with multiple time scales and coupled energy flows, a three-stage multi-subject game model containing 0–1 variables is established, and for the definition and analysis of system safety, N-1 failures are considered, and the concept of dynamic safety domain is adopted to measure system safety. Appropriate simplifications were made for the model and it was transformed into a two-stage dynamic game model with incomplete information. Concepts such as N-1 safety criterion and safety margin are used to define the payoffs of both sides of the game, and the game equilibrium is solved to provide support for system safety prevention.

articleTitle: Back Winding Inductance Calculation Considering Housing Eddy Current Effect for Gramme-Ring-Winding High-Speed Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper highlights the necessary consideration for the eddy current effect inside the housing of the grammering-winding high-speed motor due to its magnetic field outside the stator core. The back winding inductance is calculated considering the eddy current effect of the housing and the accuracy is verified, compared with FEM analysis. The analytical model is more accurate than the calculation without considering the eddy current effect.

articleTitle: Impact of Sampling and Neuron Configurations on Neural Networks for PMSM Model Order Reduction in Field-Circuit Coupling Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The field-circuit coupling model is widely used in studying motor drive systems due to its excellent capability to consider nonlinear factors. However, the finite element analysis (FEA) part of this model is highly time-consuming. To reduce simulation time while preserving the accuracy of the finite element model, this paper introduces a method to build a reduced order model (ROM) based on artificial neural networks (ANNs) by data sampled from FEA. Two sampling strategies are proposed and evaluated, which are current-intensive sampling (CIS) and angle-intensive sampling (AIS). Different ANN structures are constructed and trained to examine how neuron configurations affect the ANN's performance. It is found that the optimal neuron configurations under AIS mode demonstrates a better fitting capability for nonlinear factors, suitable for constructing ROM of neural networks.

articleTitle: Operational Risk Assessment of New Power System with Wind Power Integration Considering Inertia Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Under energy conservation, emission reduction and green sustainable development, massive renewable energy is linked to the power grid, which reduces the system inertia level. Furthermore, the inertial support capacity is weakened, leading to severe challenges in system stability. A new power system operation risk assessment method with wind power access considering inertia response is proposed to evaluate the operation risk of a new power system. Firstly, the wind power output uncertainty model is selected, choosing the non-temporal Monte Carlo method to sample the wind power output. Secondly, combined with the characteristics of the power system inertia response and the fault propagation process, a novel operational risk assessment method for power systems with wind power access considering inertia response is established while considering the risk indicators of voltage overrun severity, line overload severity and loss load severity, the initial frequency change severity index is added, and the weights of each index are calculated by the hierarchical analysis method. Finally, using the IEEE 39 system as a study, the risk assessment of the new power system with and without virtual inertia effects with wind power access is carried out respectively, and compared with the assessment value of the power system without wind power access, the model's feasibility is verified.

articleTitle: Learning Based Coordinated Voltage Control in PV Rich Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As the proportion of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation in the distribution network gradually increases, the resulting voltage regulation problem becomes increasingly complex. In this paper, a voltage control method based on Recurrent Deep Reinforcement Learning (RDRL) is proposed to achieve the cooperative operation of different voltage management devices. Starting from the action logic and control rules of On-Load Tap Changer (OLTC) and the principle of voltage regulation by PV inverters through reactive power compensation, this paper analyses the cooperative operation mechanism of these two devices in the distribution network and points out the problems that may occur when there is a lack of cooperation. To address this problem, this paper uses the Recurrent Markov Decision Process (RMDP) algorithm to achieve synergistic voltage control of OLTC and PV inverters by controlling the reactive power output of PV inverter clusters. In the technical method section, this paper describes the RMDP model considering entropy and transforms the voltage control problem into an RMDP problem. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper, the proposed RMDP algorithm is simulated and tested under strong photovoltaic fluctuations using the IEEE-33 node distribution network model. The test results show that the RMDP algorithm can effectively collaborate with the OLTC and PV inverters for voltage control, reduce the number of OLTC tap actions, reduce loss of the distribution network, and keep the voltage within the permissible range.

articleTitle: Peak Load Shaving in Virtual Power Plants Utilizing Mixed Integer Linear Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a virtual power plant (VPP) peak load shaving control strategy that takes into account both safety and economic factors, aiming to reduce operational costs for the power system. By employing mixed integer linear programming (MILP), the strategy minimizes energy and demand charges, effectively shaving peak load demands. It optimizes embedded energy resources (EERs), including distributed energy storage (DES) and renewable energy sources (RES), to decrease load during peak times. Additionally, demand response (DR) is utilized during peak periods to limit the use of consumers' electric water heaters (EWH), heat pumps (HP), and baseboard heater (BBH). The results demonstrate that the proposed control strategy can shave up to three daily load peaks, meeting the requirements for safety and reliability while enhancing the economic benefits for power companies and consumers.

articleTitle: Robust Optimal Charging Guidance Strategy for Electric Logistics Vehicles under EVs-Traffic-Distribution Collaborative Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The growing trend of electric logistic vehicle (ELV) is bringing the coupling relationship between the traffic network (TN) and the power distribution network (PDN) to a new level, while the unordered charging of electric vehicles poses a significant impact on the security of the power grid. To address this issue, this paper introduces the concept of coordinated optimization for electric logistics vehicle charging guidance con-sidering the uncertainty of renewable energy generation and load. A traffic-distribution coupled network model based on graph theory is established and then transformed into a two-stage robust optimization problem. The upper stage focuses on electric vehicle charging guidance, while the lower stage is dedicated to optimizing power allocation in the distribution network under the worst-case scenarios. The proposed model is then solved iteratively using the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm after linearization. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed methodology is validated through a case study involving the coupling of traffic and power distribution networks, and a comprehensive comparison of different charging strategies is presented.

articleTitle: Co-optimized Scheduling of Multi-Microgrids and Active Distribution Network Considering Leasing Shared Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Energy storage is widely used to smooth out new energy fluctuations, but the investment cost and the O&M cost of energy storage equipment are very high. Furthermore, the varying demand-side power consumption behaviors will lead to low equipment utilization and waste of energy storage resources. Aiming at the above problems, a co-optimized scheduling method of multi-microgrids and active distribution network (ADN) considering leasing shared energy storage (SES) is proposed. Firstly, a multi-principal energy trading framework is constructed. Secondly, a cooperative scheduling model of multi-microgrids and ADN is built and decomposed into a two-stage problem. In the first stage, the objective is minimizing the total social operating cost, and the trading power between microgrids (MGs) is captured. In the second stage, the Nash bargaining model is used to achieve a fair distribution of benefits among multiple subjects. Finally, the proposed method is simulated and validated by using the improved IEEE 33-bus system. The simulation results show that the proposed method effectively improves the utilization of energy storage, promotes the local consumption of renewable energy, and realizes the win-win benefit of multiple subjects.

articleTitle: Rotor Displacement Detection of Magnetic Bearing by Using Gradient Descent Algorithm with Differential Coil Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: To improve the integration level and reduce the cost due to the need of individual displacement sensors for active magnetic bearing (AMB) system, the self-sensing of rotor displacement is a promising technique and need further improvement in the detection accuracy. In this paper, an improved rotor displacement detection method is proposed by using the gradient descent algorithm with differential coil currents. Firstly, the instantaneous slope of coil current ripples for a two-phase three-bridge switching power amplifier is accurately measured for self-sensing. Secondly, two-phase currents of differential coil in the same degree of freedom (DOF) are synchronously sampled to double the number of data points, and the algorithm gradient descent algorithm is included to realize the self-sensing displacement detection. Finally, the suspension experiment based on self-sensing control is carried out on the test platform of 4-DOF AMB platform, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Integrating Responsive Electric Bus Chargers into Volt/Var Regulation of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The controllable reactive power compensation resources in the power system are facing problems such as insufficient quantity, relatively slow speed, as well as discontinuous regulation characteristics, leading to increasing network power loss and over-limit voltages. There is an urgent need to explore economic and fast reactive power response resources. Electric bus (EB) charging is regular and controllable, and the EB charger (EBC) has a reactive power regulation capability that gives it the ability to serve as an economical and reliable volt/var support for power system. This paper explores the reactive power regulation potential of EBC and applies it to the power system automatic voltage control (AVC). Firstly, the reactive power regulation capability of EBCs is quantitatively evaluated based on the converter operating characteristics and aggregated as a voltage reactive power regulation resource for the transmission system. Then, the reactive power regulation capability of EBCs is integrated into AVC and a multi-objective volt/var optimization model based on OPF considering aggregated responsive EBCs is established. Ultimately, the numerical experiment utilizing a modified IEEE 30-bus test system are performed to confirm the practicality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation on Electromagnetic Vibration Characteristics of Induction Motor Fed by Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this paper, an induction motor with the slot combination of 30/22 is taken as an example to study the vibration characteristics under different carrier frequencies, loads and speeds. First, an analytical model of electromagnetic force waves considering the harmonic current of the inverter is established to analyze the source of electromagnetic force waves. Then, a comparative analysis of the current, flux density, and vibration spectra under sinusoidal and variable frequency power supplies is conducted. Finally, the vibration characteristics of the studied motor under different carrier frequencies, loads and speeds are experimentally analyzed. The results show that as the carrier frequency increases, the vibration is effectively suppressed, but the suppression effect gradually weakens. Compared with the carrier frequency, the load change has little effect on the vibration. During the speed regulation process, although the amplitude of the rotor slot harmonic flux density changes little, the vibration weakens because its frequency gradually moves away from the natural frequency; this shows that optimizing the motor from the aspect of avoiding the main harmonic frequency of the natural frequency can also effectively suppress the vibration.

articleTitle: An Incremental Non-Intrusive Load Disaggregation Model Considering Dynamic Changes of Appliances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In recent years, substantial increase in electricity demand has led to dynamic loads in the grid. The unpredictability of these incremental loads often hampers traditional load disaggregation techniques. Thus, we propose an incremental non-intrusive disaggregation model. It aims to effectively disaggregate additional appliances. We systematically outline the pros and cons of existing NILM techniques, and then use a sequence-to-point model combined with transfer learning to disaggregate the incremental loads. Validation is conducted on the REDD dataset. Results demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed model in disaggregating incremental loads.

articleTitle: Capacity Optimization Configuration Method for Energy Storage Considering Emergency Support
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In recent years, the frequency of extreme global disaster events has increased, leading to large-scale outages in distribution systems and causing significant socioeconomic losses. Energy storage systems are crucial for ensuring the stability of electricity supply; however, focusing solely on disaster scenarios results in low energy storage utilization. Therefore, it is essential to comprehensively address the energy storage configuration problem in both normal and disaster scenarios. This study first analyzes the benefits of energy storage participation in spot markets and emergency power supply situations, constructing a revenue-risk model based on portfolio theory. Subsequently, it establishes an optimization configuration model for multi-scenario energy storage participation, considering both planning and operation. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to energy storage participation in a single spot market, multi-scenario applications yield higher revenue and lower investment risk.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Cost Endplate Using Same Rotor Core Silicon Steel Sheet for Interior Permanent Magnet Motors in Domestic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-cost rotor endplate of interior permanent magnet motors (IPM) for domestic applications. The novelty of the proposed solution lies in utilizing the same rotor core silicon steel sheet as the endplate, so as to eliminate the cost of dedicated rotor endplates. However, since the proposed endplates and rotor core are the same, the magnets can move axially without the limitation of the endplates when their magnet slots coincide. To prevent axial displacement of the magnets, the proposed endplates are rotated axially at a certain mechanical angle concerning the rotor core. In such a solution, the endplates cannot be mounted to the rotor core using rivets since the original rivet holes between them no longer coincide. To solve this problem, additional rivet holes are designed so that some rivet holes between them can coincide after the rotation of the proposed endplates. Besides, due to the high permeability of the endplate, flux barriers in the rotor endplates are studied to mitigate flux leakage at the rotor end. Specifically, the design considerations of the proposed rotor endplate are investigated, including the rotation angle, rivet holes, and flux barriers. Two IPM motors adopting the proposed low-cost endplates at different rotation angles are developed and compared with the conventional IPM motor by using finite element analysis. It shows that the overall performance (back-EMF, cogging torque, efficiency, and complexity of rotor structure) of the IPM motors adopting the low-cost endplates at a proper rotation angle is comparable to the conventional design.

articleTitle: Design of A Novel Primary Permanent Magnet Linear Machine with Low Thrust Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to reduce thrust ripple, this paper proposes a new primary permanent magnet linear machine with uneven pole (UP-PPMLM). Firstly, the proposed structure and advantages compared to conventional structure are introduced. Then, the expressions of air-gap flux density by permanent magnets (PMs) and armature reaction are derived. Finally, by using finite element method (FEM), the new topology reasonability is proved. Meanwhile, the performances of proposed machines are compared to conventional topology, and the result confirms the electromagnetic performances of the proposed machine have been greatly improved.

articleTitle: Workload Scheduling of Data Center Based on Electricity Price and Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and information technology, the scale of data center has increased rapidly. As a high-energy-consuming industry, data centers consume huge amounts of electricity, and their electricity expenses account for about 70% of the operating costs. Therefore, there is an urgent need for data centers to change their electricity usage behavior to reduce electricity bills. In addition, the workload of the data center is transferable in the time dimension. Based on this, this paper firstly constructs an energy consumption model based on workload transfer to characterize the energy consumption of the data center. Then, the LSTM-based prediction model for electricity price and data center's workload is built. Lastly, the load optimization scheduling model of data center based on electricity price and load forecasting is applied to minimize electricity cost.

articleTitle: Fractional Modeling and Analysis of Inductance for Thrust Magnetic Bearings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Thrust magnetic bearings (TMB) are typically of solid structure, with windings wound around. There is prominent eddy current effect, which results in frequency-varying inductance of the TMB winding. The traditional models cannot accurately describe the time-varying characteristics of the TMB coil. Considering the eddy current effect can improve the accuracy of the model, but there are still nonlinear factors, which still make it difficult to accurately describe the response of the system over the full operating frequency range. Therefore, this paper proposes a modeling method for the TMB Inductance based on fractional order elements, and the fractional order TMB model is established using parameter identification methods based on the measured TMB inductance and resistance values to tackle the nonlinear factors. The accuracy of the model is verified by simulations and experimental tests with current ripple under different switching frequencies.

articleTitle: Online Monitoring for the Safety of Insulation of Inverter-Fed Equipment Under Varying Working Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The online condition method for the safety of insulation can give prognosis for potential failure in inverter-fed equipment such as motors, which can avoid the huge losses caused by the unexpected failure. In the existing methods, the equivalent impedance of the stator winding is estimated in frequency domain by measuring the terminal voltages and leakage current. Because the output voltage of the inverter has many harmonics, the frequency resolution of the monitoring method should be as high as 1~10 Hz to distinguish different harmonics. For the traditional method such as FFT (Fast Fourier Transform), the window length should be very long. If the fundamental frequency of the inverter-fed machine changes in the window in varying work condition, the existing method cannot estimate the impedance parameters accurately. Therefore, a sliding window matrix pencil method is proposed to solve this problem. The online experimental results prove that it can estimate the groundwall and phase-to-phase insulation parameters accurately in varying work condition.

articleTitle: Locating and Sizing of Charging Stations Based on Electric Vehicle Load Forecasting Considering Road Network Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In recent years, electric vehicles(EVs) has developed fast. As EVs have both mobile load and transportation attributes, disordered EV charging will influence the power grid and transportation network at the same time. Therefore, through reasonable prediction of the load of EVs and reasonable planning of charging stations, positive effect will show on the power grid and transportation network. Firstly, the traffic network matrix is established and the origin and destination of EVs are analyzed by OD analysis method. Then, the driving path of the EV is simulated by the Monte Carlo analysis method, the charging demand of the vehicle is determined by the electric quantity of the EV, and the charging requirement of each station is predicted according to the position of the charging station. Finally, taking the loss of the distribution network to the minimum as the optimization objective, the distribution network loss under the power flow constraint is calculated, and the location and capacity of the charging station are determined considering the distribution network loss and the load of EVs charging. Taking the actual transportation network of a city as an example, the validity of the model proposed in this paper is verified.

articleTitle: Laddered Carbon Trading-based Scheduling for Integrated Electricity-Gas Systems with Hydrogen Injection Considering Hydrogen Mixed Gas Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Hydrogen is recognized as a clean and appealing energy carrier that offers significant flexibility enhancements to power systems. This paper proposes a laddered carbon trading-based energy scheduling model for integrated electricity-gas system (IEGS) with hydrogen injection considering the combustion properties of hydrogen mixed gas turbine (HMGT). The power-to-hydrogen, carbon capture, utilization and storage facility and laddered carbon trading are considered to reduce the carbon emission. Then, a simplified HMGT combustion model based on the system thermodynamics is developed. A quasi-steady-state operation model for gas system with hydrogen injection is also introduced and solved by a convex relaxation method. Case studies illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Air-Cooled Cooling Method for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Heat Pipe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes an innovative air-cooled heat pipe cooling (ACHP) method, where the heat pipes are integrated into the stator end-winding of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). This approach makes full use of the inactive space in the end-winding, effectively reducing the impact of heat pipe losses on the system, and significantly improves the operating environment and reliability of the motor. Compared to traditional forced air-cooled cooling (FACC) systems, this method effectively enhances the cooling performance and power density of the motor. Additionally, the paper employs a simplified iterative optimization design method based on a lumped-parameter thermal network (LPTN) to optimize the dimensions of the heat pipes in the ACHP system. In motor thermal management, LPTN is widely used for simulating the temperature field of motors due to its simplicity and efficiency. By establishing a three-dimensional fluid-solid coupling model, and comparing the temperature results of the ACHP system with those of the FACC system. The results show that the maximum winding temperature in the ACHP system was reduced by 35.6°C compared to the FACC system.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Control of Active Magnetic Bearings-Flexible Rotor Based on NSGA-II Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the active magnetic bearings (AMBs)-flexible rotor system, decentralized PID control is usually adopted to achieve stability control. In this paper, a multi-objective control based on recursive open-loop adaptive control (MO-ROLAC) algorithm is designed on the basis of PID control, which can realize multi-objective control including vibration displacement, bearing transmission force and control current. In order to simplify the selection of weight coefficients in the controller, a multi-objective optimization algorithm NSGA-II is introduced. Simulation results show that the controller designed in this paper has obvious control effect and can simultaneously reduce vibration displacement, transmission force and control current.

articleTitle: FCS-MPC of IPMSM Based on Online Parameter Identification Under Demagnetization Condition of Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM), the permanent magnet can easily demagnetize under high temperature and high-speed conditions due to the action of demagnetizing current. The stator resistance and stator inductance also vary with the operation of the motor. These parameter variations hinder the optimal performance of finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC). This paper proposes a Finite Control Set Model Predictive Current Control (FCS-MPCC) based on parameter identification methods for interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSM), which can implement model current predictive control under conditions of parameter variations. The recursive least squares (RLS) method with a forgetting factor was used to achieve online real-time identification of four electrical parameters, namely stator resistance, d-axis inductance, q-axis inductance, and magnetic flux. The identified parameters are updated in real-time into the model predictive control, achieving FCS-MPC under conditions of magnet demagnetization. Simulation results show that, compared to conventional FCS-MPC strategies based on motor nominal parameters, the proposed method reduces current prediction errors and effectively reduces motor speed fluctuation under conditions of magnet demagnetization. This paper contributes to expanding the application of IPMSM under conditions leading to magnet demagnetization, such as high temperature or high-speed states.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Energy Management Strategy for Micro-Energy Grids Considering Dynamic Pricing Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper presents a low-carbon energy management strategy for microgrids that uses dynamic pricing mechanisms to balance the interests of microgrid operators and users. The strategy involves using carbon capture power-to-gas devices and ground source heat pumps to reduce system carbon emissions. The Information Gap Decision Theory addresses the output uncertainty of renewable energy. The strategy has an upper layer that decides on energy prices and device output based on market prices and user demand and a lower layer that utilizes demand response to decide on load demand based on energy prices. The bilevel nonlinear model is transformed into a single-layer mixed-integer linear programming model for solution, and a case study verifies the strategy's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Decoupled Partitioning of Active and Reactive Power for Voltage Control in Distribution System Based on Generalized Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The large-scale integration of distributed photovoltaics (PV) is prone to reverse power flow in distribution systems, resulting in voltage exceeding limits at distribution buses, which restricts the consumption of distributed PV. To address this, this paper proposes a method of decoupled partitioning of reactive and active power for voltage control in distribution systems based on generalized distance. Firstly, consider both active/reactive power-voltage sensitivity and impedance distance to partition the distribution system into active power partitions and reactive power partitions, respectively. Then, following the strategy of prioritizing reactive power adjustment before active power, control voltage within partitions, thus resolving voltage exceeding limits. Finally, simulations based on IEEE 33 bus system verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved Frequency Response Model for Asynchronously Interconnected Power Systems Considering Voltage Changes Due to Load Variations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Due to the reduction in the capacity of synchronous generator units and the gradual transition of synchronous grids to asynchronously interconnected systems, frequency stability has become increasingly critical for the safe and stable operation of power systems. However, existing equivalent model methods used for frequency analysis do not consider the impact of voltage changes during frequency events, leading to inaccurate calculations of frequency deviation. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved frequency response model (IFR) suitable for asynchronously interconnected grids that takes voltage changes into account. The IFR adds load flow calculations to the initial frequency response model, accurately calculating the actual power disturbance in the system and thereby more accurately predicting the maximum frequency deviation and quasi-steady-state frequency. The correctness of the model is verified in PSCAD/EMTDC on a four machine two area system (4G2A). The simulation results show that the improved frequency response model can better represent the frequency dynamics of the interconnected grid, with the relative error of the maximum frequency deviation reduced by up to 35.24%.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation for Photovoltaic Power Station based Multi-state Models of Photovoltaic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As the scale of photovoltaic power stations continues to expand, the number of internal elements has increased, and the series of parallel structures between elements has become more complex. The reliability of photovoltaic power stations has become an issue that cannot be ignored. However, the current reliability assessment of photovoltaic stations mostly focuses on analyzing element faults, lacking the division of element operating states. Therefore, this paper proposes a reliability evaluation method for photovoltaic power station based multi-state models of photovoltaic arrays (PAs). Firstly, the PAs which are the key elements of photovoltaic power stations are divided into different states. Secondly, a multi-state reliability model of PA is built based on the Markov process. Then the reliability indexes of PA are proposed from both time and overall perspectives. Finally, the reliability evaluation results under different states are analyzed in the case study.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability of Grid-Forming Converters Under Fault Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The threshold virtual impedance (TVI) method is gaining significant research interest for limiting current in grid-forming (GFM) converters under fault conditions. This method is valued for its ability to maintain voltage source behavior during such faults. However, sequence extraction and negative-sequence control (NSC) are often overlooked in small-signal stability assessments under these conditions. This paper develops a small-signal impedance model for GFM converters based on the TVI current limitation method during fault conditions. Using developed small-signal impedance model, the impact of NSC on system stability during faults is analyzed. Additionally, key TVI parameters, such as the low-pass filter (LPF) cutoff frequency and the impedance ratio X/R are examined. The findings suggest that NSC, a lower LPF cutoff frequency, and a lower X/R ratio enhance system stability under fault conditions. However, a lower cutoff frequency may not effectively limit fault currents, and a lower X/R ratio can lead to reduced voltage magnitude during faults. Time-domain simulations validate these analytical results.

articleTitle: Assessment of Demand Response Capability of Industrial Users with Continuous Processes Considering Multi-Time Scales
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Traditional assessment of demand response capability of industrial users typically consider a single time scale, making it difficult to comprehensively assess the demand response capability of industrial users across different time scales. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for assessing industrial user's demand response that takes multi-time scales into account. First, the paper analyzes the three production characteristics of industrial users: supply reliability, periodicity, and continuity, as well as the differences in demand response capabilities of industrial users at different time scales. Then it constructs a framework for assessing demand response capability that considers multi-time scales. Following this, short-term and long-term demand response capability assessment models are proposed. Finally, using a case study of an actual cement plant, the paper applies the proposed assessment model to study and analyze the short-term and long-term demand response capabilities, verifying the reliability of the model and providing industrial users with more accurate decision support for load adjustment.

articleTitle: Impedance Modeling of Thermal Power Generator Considering Electromechanical Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Thermal power generators (TPGs) play a significant role in the stability of renewable-integrated power system. In the current impedance modeling and analysis of renewable energy delivery systems, the TPGs and their shaft system models, which are integral components of the system, are often neglected. This paper employs a segmented concentrated four-mass-spring shaft system model to establish an impedance model for TPGs that accounts for the mechanical system of the shaft. The analysis examines the interplay between the electrical and mechanical systems. Furthermore, it analyzes how mechanical disturbances affect the stator's output voltage and current, thereby influencing the unit's impedance.

articleTitle: Control Strategy for CSI-Fed PMSM Based on Linear Matrix Inequalities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The current source inverter (CSI) fed permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) system is a high-order system due to the inclusion of filter capacitors, which complicates the tuning of control parameters. To solve this problem, a control structure based on state feedback and a servo compensator is proposed, and linear matrix inequalities (LMI) are employed to describe the pole placement problem. By the convenient calculation of LMI, the control parameters that meet the performance specifications can be obtained easily. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of this strategy. Compared to traditional approaches, it not only delivers improved dynamic performance and load disturbance rejection but also effectively suppresses current and torque ripples.

articleTitle: Efficient Operation and Disaggregation Method for Distributed Resources with Risk Consideration and Zonotope Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The popularity of distributed resources (DRs) on the distribution network (DN) side provides great potential for interaction with the power grid. However, the volume of resources is not enough to support their independent participation in the market, so the aggregation and unified scheduling of DRs has become a hot topic in current research. This paper proposes a DRs aggregation, regulation, and instruction decomposition method for energy communities. It is worth noting that this study, based on Zonotope and conditional value at risk (CVaR) theory, solves the problem of concurrent regulation of user-side resources and community resources, and weakens the impact of external environmental uncertainty on system regulation. Through simulation experiments and case studies, the significant results of this method in the economic benefits of energy community entity and user entities are verified.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Economic Dispatch of Coordinated Power-Transportation Systems with Electric Vehicles and Hydrogen Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The integrated power-hydrogen energy system can effectively utilize renewable energy sources to replace traditional fossil fuels, thereby promoting the development of sustainable transportation. However, the complex interactions among electricity, hydrogen, and transportation pose significant challenges for the effective dispatch of integrated systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a comprehensive management and trading scheme for power-hydrogen integration, specifically designed for charging battery electric vehicles and refueling fuel cell electric vehicles, while incorporating stochastic optimization to account for the uncertainty of renewable energy active output. The proposed method demonstrates significant positive outcomes through testing on an improved IEEE 33-node distribution network and a real-world based transportation network in case study.

articleTitle: Parameter Tuning of LCC-HVDC for Providing Active Frequency Support in Asynchronously Interconnected Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Line-Commutated Converter based High Voltage Direct Current (LCC-HVDC) can be used to provide frequency support for to one end of the asynchronously interconnected systems (AIS) owing to its strong power control capabilities. However, existing research overlooks the impact of providing frequency support on the system at the other end, potentially leading to significant frequency drop. This paper proposes a parameter tuning method that ensures an appropriate level of frequency support without jeopardizing the frequency response of the system at the remote end. Firstly, the characteristics of two main control schemes, namely Droop Control (DRC) and Virtual Inertia Control (VIC), used for AIS frequency support, are analyzed. Then this paper demonstrated that, from the perspectives of frequency nadir, DRC can effectively substitute for VIC without affecting the initial Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) while improving the quasi-steady-state frequency. Furthermore, a DRC-based parameter tuning method of LCC-HVDC is proposed, which ensures a reasonable level of frequency support. Finally, simulation results on a modified four-generator two-area (4G2A) power system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Power System Dynamic Simulation with High-Penetration Renewable Generation via Time-Step Adjustment Based on ETFBs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the widespread integration of renewable energy sources (REs), the number of power system scenarios to be analyzed has increased significantly, and the system structure has become increasingly complex, which increases the computational burden of power system dynamic simulations and leads to substantial computation time. Therefore, there is an urgent need to improve the efficiency of dynamic simulation to meet the requirements of advanced applications. The uEITSA method adopts a fixed system time-step in the overall simulation, which makes it challenging to balance simulation accuracy and efficiency. Therefore, a system time-step adjustment strategy is proposed in this paper to optimize the uEITSA method, implemented in the open-source Simulation Toolkit for Electrical Power Systems (STEPS). Firstly, the system time-step adjustment strategy based on elementary transfer function blocks (ETFBs) is introduced. Secondly, the implementation of the proposed strategy in STEPS software is described in detail. Finally, the simplified Shandong Power Grid model is tested to demonstrate that the proposed system time-step adjustment strategy can improve simulation efficiency without jeopardizing simulation accuracy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Vibration Suppression Control for Direct-Drive Flexible Manipulators Based on PMSM Self-Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In flexible manipulator systems driven directly by permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM), residual vibration following servo positioning has a detrimental effect on the precision and efficiency of industrial operations. This study proposes an adaptive vibration suppression control strategy based on PMSM self-sensing, which is founded upon the dynamics model of direct-drive flexible manipulators. This strategy permits the estimation of vibration frequency and damping coefficient without the necessity for supplementary vibration sensors and fast Fourier transform (FFT). The parameters of the input shaper are dynamically adjusted by means of adaptive frequency and damping coefficient identification. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Modeling of PMSM Based on LUT in Electrical Drive Real-time Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Hardware in the loop (HIL) is an advanced testing method for simulating electrical drive systems. As an important component of electrical drive systems, the modeling accuracy of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) will directly affect the real-time simulation effect, while the control algorithm needs to be developed and optimized based on accurate motor models. However, most modeling of PMSM used in HIL testing for electric drive systems adopt the basic linear model, ignoring the nonlinear relationship between magnetic flux and current caused by hysteresis saturation and cross-coupling. This paper studies the nonlinear modeling method of PMSMs and proposes an interpolation algorithm selection method based on the lookup table (LUT) method. The error between interpolation results and finite element data under different algorithms is compared to improve interpolation accuracy while ensuring the real-time performance of HIL in the smallest possible table size. Finally, by building a HIL testing platform, it was verified that the nonlinear model has high accuracy while ensuring real-time simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Switchgear Fault Warning Based on Improved HHO-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Switchgear is a key component of the safe and stable operation of the power supply system. If a switchgear malfunction occurs, it not only interferes with the normal power supply process, but also may trigger a serious safety accident. To ensure the safe and reliable operation of switchgear and to minimize the risk of potential accidents, it is essential to establish a mechanism capable of accurately forecasting changes in the switchgear's operational status and to implement an effective fault early warning system. As a result, an efficient intelligent fault warning model IHHO-LSTM is proposed by combining the improved Harris hawk algorithm with the long and short-term memory neural network, which introduces adaptive inertia weights, nonlinear escape energy factor, and Tent chaotic mapping to improve the original Harris hawk algorithm, which are designed to improve the algorithm's global searching ability and accelerate the convergence speed so as to enhance the overall efficiency of the solving process. LSTM neural network models are excellent in the field of prediction, but their performance is largely dependent on the hyperparameter settings. Traditional hyperparameter optimization methods are time-consuming and inefficient. To enhance predictive accuracy, this research employs an improved Harris Hawk Optimization algorithm to swiftly identify the optimal hyperparameters for the LSTM model. The method is used to analyze the historical data of switchgear operation in a city in North China, and by analyzing the experimental results, it can be seen that the fault early warning model is able to accurately predict the switchgear state volume data and provide fault early warning for it.

Author Keywords: Long and short-term memory neural networks

articleTitle: Bidding Strategy of Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage in Power Spot Market Considering the Impacts of Coal Price Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The fluctuation of coal prices significantly affects the cost dynamics of traditional thermal power in the electricity market, which can affect the market price of electricity through marginal costs. Moreover, the renewable energy source (RES), such as wind turbine (WT), photovoltaic (PV), and energy storage (ES), grows rapidly, which can be allowed to bid in the power spot market as a whole. Therefore, a bidding strategy of WT-PV-ES generator participation in the spot market is proposed in this paper, where the uncertainties of coal prices are considered. Firstly, the uncertainty of clearing price in electricity spot market is analyzed with unified clearing and clustering method proposed, which considers coal spot and annual market differences. Then, a stochastic optimization model is established considering the joint bidding of WT-PV-ES for clearing prices uncertainty scenarios. The proposed method aims to obtain a bidding strategy for the joint power generator that maximizes expected revenues in the spot market. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, a case study and discussion are provided. The effectiveness of proposed model is validated through the results.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a High-Speed Permanent Magnet BLAC Motor for Hand Dryer Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In hand dryer application, high efficiency is preferred to decrease energy consumption, and low torque ripple is crucial to reduce the motor's vibration and noise. This paper presents three designs for a 1 kW, 83 krpm permanent magnet brushless AC machine for hand dryer application, namely initial design, less-PM design, and more-PM design. The initial design is used as a benchmark, and the two other designs are proposed to enhance the efficiency and minimize the torque ripple by increasing the armature inductance. Using two-dimensional finite-element analysis (FEA), the electromagnetic performance including back EMF, cogging torque, average torque, torque ripple, losses, and efficiency is investigated and compared under no load and load conditions. In terms of efficiency, all three machine designs achieve an efficiency above 90%, meeting the target design requirements. On top of that, the less-PM design effectively reduces the torque ripple by 25% and rotor eddy current loss by 34%, while the more-PM design achieves a significant reduction in rotor eddy current loss by 45% and the torque ripple by 10%, making both designs optimal for improved performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: Critical Nodes Detection and Dynamic Vulnerability Analysis in Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Due to the continual growth of electrical grids to meet increasing demand, integrating electronic devices and new generation units has become a common practice within electrical power systems. These modifications in network topology can introduce new vulnerable nodes. Consequently, there is a growing need for robust strategies to accurately quantify and assess the vulnerability of these evolving power systems. Many existing methodologies primarily leverage topological information to enhance the understanding of system vulnerabilities. In response to these challenges, this research introduces a hybrid methodology for detecting and validating vulnerable nodes. This novel approach combines a dedicated vulnerability metric to pinpoint nodes of critical significance with applying transient stability analysis to validate these nodes systematically. Through this innovative approach, this work contributes to the comprehensive understanding of vulnerability within electrical power systems and offers practical insights into enhancing system resilience.

articleTitle: High-Accuracy Analytical Method for AC Copper Loss in Flat Wire Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper contrasts 1D, 2D analytical approaches and Mellor method for computing winding AC losses with Finite Element Analysis (FEA), but these methods solely account for the influence of the armature reaction field. Building upon this foundation, a new approach called finite element method magnetics(FEMM) is introduced to incorporate the impact of the reaction field generated by permanent magnets. This enhancement significantly diminishes the computational inaccuracy of the AC loss, particularly in scenarios where the armature reaction field is less pronounced.

articleTitle: Current Sensorless Deadbeat Predictive Control for Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a current sensorless permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive scheme based on deadbeat predictive control in which a space vector pulse modulator is introduced for feedback currents to track reference currents accurately. Current sensors are omitted by replacing actual currents with predicted currents, thus only a position sensor is needed and a low-cost servo system is achieved. PI control is adopted for the speed loop. Simulation comparisons between control with current sensors and current sensorless control under external disturbances or parameter inconsistency are conducted to indicate that the performance of current sensorless control is almost the same as that of control with current sensors when the prediction model is accurate.

articleTitle: Reducing Electricity Fees by Smart Building Energy Management: A Case Study in Shenzhen with PEDF System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The difference between peak and valley electricity prices becomes even larger and various types of power regulation modes such as virtual power plant gradually emerge. In this context, flexibly regulating building loads by building energy management systems can help users reduce electricity costs. This paper proposes a building energy control strategy for an office building that uses a building energy system integrated with the photovoltaic, energy storage, direct current, and flexibility (PEDF) system. The control strategy optimizes scheduling of adjustable loads in buildings such as energy storage, air conditioners, charging piles, and lighting to improve the utilization of solar roof and reduce the power consumption demands during the peak period. The control strategy run continuously in the project for half a year. The results show that the average cost for electricity consumption is reduced by 66% when compared with the regular operational condition without PEDF system and is reduced by 20% when compared with the operational condition before the control strategy are implemented.

articleTitle: Total Accommodation Capability Curve for Distribution Networks with Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: To enhance the accommodation capability of the distribution network for distributed generation (DG), this paper proposes a total accommodation capability (TAC) curve for smart distribution networks with energy storage. Firstly, a mathematical model and solution algorithm for the TAC curve of smart distribution networks with energy storage are proposed. Secondly, the influence of the integration location and capacity of energy storage on the TAC curve is investigated. It is found that only the energy storage downstream of bottleneck branches affects the TAC curve. Then, measures such as increasing the capacity of energy storage downstream of bottleneck branches and expanding the capacity of the bottleneck branches are proposed to enhance the accommodation capability. Furthermore, the application of the TAC curve in guiding DG and energy storage integration as well as conductor replacement is demonstrated. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by an IEEE 33-node case. The proposed TAC curve effectively depicts the complete accommodation capability of smart distribution networks with energy storage and holds practical value for distribution network planning.

articleTitle: Calculating the Carbon Emission Flows of Power Systems Considering Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Accurate and fair carbon emission measurement is the key premise of power system decarbonization. As the improvement of the traditional carbon measuring methods based on macro statistics, Carbon emission flow (CEF) reflects the distributions of carbon emissions caused by generation in power systems. However, existing CEF measurement algorithms cannot consider the influence of market mechanism on the allocation of carbon emission responsibility under the background of the electricity markets. This paper proposes a new CEF calculation method considering various market trading forms. Based on the expanded power transmission distribution factor, the power flow and network losses are decoupled according to each trade and the CEF of each trade are respectively computed, realizing the carbon emission responsibility calculation of each entity in the electricity market. The proposed algorithm has been verified in a modified IEEE-14 bus system, showing better numerical characteristics and more reasonable calculation results, which provides a solid foundation for the accurate measurement of carbon emissions and the accurate delineation of emission reduction responsibilities.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Photovoltaic Integrated Fusion Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A novel Photovoltaic (PV) integrated fusion topology is proposed in this paper. The flyback converter is utilized to elevate low PV output voltage to the desired level of fusion topology. Accordingly, the reactive and harmonic currents can be compensated, and the generated active power from PV can also be utilized on-site. Thus, the extra grid-tied inverter for PV can be saved while maintaining the advantages of fusion topology, e.g. lower power loss and ample capacity with the simple system design. The system configuration is presented by analyzing the DC-link voltage requirements in the fusion topology. Simulation results validate the feasibility of the proposed topology, which demonstrates the potential to enhance power network stability, support renewable energy integration, and foster sustainable power system development.

articleTitle: Distributed Photovoltaic Power Siting and Capacity Sizing Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: A photovoltaic grid integration planning method that balances economy and safety is proposed for the site selection and capacity determination of distributed photovoltaic power sources accessed to the distribution grid. Considering three objectives of voltage deviation, network loss, and investment cost, a multi-objective constrained optimization model for distributed photovoltaic access distribution network is constructed with constraints of power flow, node voltage, and access capacity. A distributed photovoltaic access distribution network location and capacity optimization method based on improved particle swarm optimization is proposed. Taking the IEEE33 node distribution system as an example, simulation and comparative analysis are conducted to verify its effectiveness and feasibility.

articleTitle: A SVC Voltage Regulation Control Strategy of Active Distribution Network Based on Improved Particle Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the continuous depletion of fossil energy, the state has introduced a series of policies to aggressively pursue the development of new energy sources to protect the environment and realize sustainable development. Distributed photovoltaic is widely utilized due to its advantages of flexible installation, cleanliness and high efficiency. However, the output of distributed PV is uncertain and random. When it integrated into the distribution network on a large scale, they may alter the power flow direction, impacting the quality of power in the distribution network and potentially causing serious consequence such as voltage limit violation. To ensure stable voltage levels, this article presents a strategy for optimizing reactive power and voltage, taking into account the integration of distributed photovoltaic systems. Firstly, the paper establishes a model for the output of distributed PV and analyzes the impact of the integration on the voltage. Subsequently, it introduces the working principle of the Static Var Compensator (SVC). Aiming to reduce voltage deviations within the distribution grid, an Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm is utilized for a case study on the IEEE 33-bus system. The results validate that the proposed SVC reactive power compensation strategy can optimize the voltage and guarantee the secure and reliable functioning of the distribution grid.

articleTitle: An LLM-Assisted Framework for Synthetic Power Network Graph Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Due to privacy and security concerns surrounding actual power system structure data, many studies have focused on generating simulated power grids and providing corresponding datasets. However, existing methods and datasets often struggle with effective visualization and lack diverse power grid scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a large language model-assisted workflow for small-scale synthetic power grid generation, verification, and visualization. Moreover, by taking into account the variety of node types and connection relationships inherent in power networks, our approach aims to enhance understanding of structural characteristics through detailed feature representation. We leverage the large language model to enrich the generated power grid structure data, uncovering potential internal structures. Furthermore, we employ advanced visualization techniques to generate power structure images, facilitating analysis by human experts and supporting potential learning tasks. Our results demonstrate that the generated power grid structures align well with the properties of real-world networks, and the visual outputs effectively highlight the intricacies of these structures. The code and examples are available at https://github.com/SYLLABLE604/PG-generator.

articleTitle: Impact of Axial Shapes of Circumferential Modes on Electromagnetic Noise in Outer-Rotor Permanent-Magnet In-Wheel Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Circumferential modes are recognized as the primary contributors to electromagnetic (EM) noise of permanent-magnet (PM) in-wheel motors (IWMs), whereas their axial shapes have not been thoroughly investigated. Given the significance of axial shapes in outer-rotor (OR) structures, this paper aims to investigate the impact of axial shapes on the EM noise of a 72-slot/80-pole OR-IWM. Finite element analysis (FEA) is used to predict the main circumferential modes of the rotor. The uneven distribution of axial shapes is observed and also verified by the modal test. A coupled-field FEA model is subsequently established, demonstrating that the variation of the modal amplitude of each segment can result in significant differences in velocity responses. To reveal the impact, the circumferential mode shapes of each segment are axially reduced and expressed by the Fourier series. The findings indicate that, in addition to amplitude variation, rotor skewing also generates phase variations in mode harmonics, which should be carefully considered in the design of OR-IWMs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power System Stability: A Machine Learning Approach with SVM, Random Forest and Deep Learning Utilizing Wide Area Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As the scale and complexity of modern power systems continue to expand, the importance of system stability has become increasingly critical. To ensure the stable operation of the power system, this paper proposes a power system stability analysis and optimal control strategy based on the Wide Area Measurement System (WAMS). Initially, a novel stability evaluation method is established using WAMS data and machine learning techniques, enabling effective handling of complex power system data and providing accurate stability assessments. Following this, an optimal control strategy is designed based on the evaluation method, aimed at real-time adjustments of power resource allocation to enhance system stability and responsiveness. Simulation analyses confirm the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed approach, indicating that the optimized control strategy significantly improves the system's performance under disturbances. This paper presents an innovative method for the stable operation of integrated power systems, contributing to the enhancement of power supply quality within the grid and ensuring the safe and efficient operation of the overall power system.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment and Risk Analysis of Virtual Power Plant Scheduling with Diverse Load Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Receiving-end distribution networks are facing increasing scarcity of flexibility regulation resources, while virtual power plant (VPP) can effectively aggregate diverse loads such as central air-conditioning, electric vehicles and rooftop photovoltaic users to participate in the demand response, thus effectively improving the scheduling flexibility of the distribution network. Considering the uncertain response of the diverse load resources, the VPP scheduling decision model is established by using fuzzy chance constraint planning, and the response reliable capacity and response capacity reliability are defined to measure the VPP scheduling reliability. On this basis, the VPP scheduling risk assessment method is proposed based on fuzzy simulation technology, and then the scheduling risk is analyzed under different confidence levels and different penalty coefficients. The results validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: Enhanced Condition Assessment of IGBTs Through 3D Segmented Reconstruction Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: The condition assessment method of the Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) devices is investigated in this paper. Simulation models in 2D and 3D are constructed based on the finite element models, and the differences between the two models are compared.
