To improve the accuracy of the 2D model and meet the requirements of digital twin technology, based on the 3D simulation physical model to correct the 2D computational results, the 3D segmented reconstruction method was proposed. By constructing a mathematical model, the output results of the 2D and 3D models were segmented and fitted to derive the corresponding relationship formulas for each segment. Using these formulas to optimize the computational results of the 2D model significantly improved the simulation speed while ensuring high accuracy, meeting the real-time and accuracy requirements of digital twin technology.

articleTitle: Optimal Economic Dispatch Strategy for Microgrids Considering Distributed Energy Storage Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: User-side distributed energy storage, as a flexible demand response resource, possesses excellent source-load interaction characteristics and can effectively interact with the power grid. However, currently in China, user-side distributed energy storage resources often face difficulties in directly participating in grid regulation due to factors such as dispersed geographical distribution, small individual installed capacity, and uncertain output time. To address this issue, this paper proposes an optimal economic dispatch strategy for microgrids that considers distributed energy storage aggregation. First, a distributed energy storage aggregator is introduced to manage scattered user-side distributed energy storage resources in a scaled manner, and the scheduling potential of distributed energy storage in each time period is assessed based on consumer psychology theory. Subsequently, a multi-objective optimal dispatch model for microgrids is constructed, which takes into account both economic and environmental aspects. The multi-objective optimization problem is transformed into a single-objective optimization problem using the weighted assignment method, and the CPLEX solver is employed to solve the problem. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method in this paper are verified through a microgrid test system.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Non-Intrusive Load Disaggregation Considering Continuous Power Appliances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) can achieve device-level event detection and energy disaggregation by utilizing meter data at power entrance, paving the way for a smart energy consumption future. However, the presence of continuously variable device (CVD) poses challenges for accurate event detection and disaggregation of other devices. Therefore, this paper proposes a NILM model and method focusing on continuous power feature. It analyzes the power change intensity within sliding windows to accurately determine the switching moments of finite-state device (FSD). Subsequently, a deep learning-based load disaggregation method predicts FSD power consumption. By stepwise striping FSD and noise, the CVD power consumption is obtained. Scenario-based simulation results validate the effectiveness of the method to achieve precise event detection and all-type load energy consumption disaggregation.

articleTitle: A Data-Physics Fusion-Based Approach to Power System Equivalent Inertia Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In order to solve the error problem of the traditional inertia assessment method, a power system equivalent inertia assessment method incorporating machine learning technology is proposed. First, a physical model of single-machine equivalence is used, combined with a convolutional neural network (CNN) with self-adaptive and learning capabilities as a machine learning model. Second, the strongly correlated feature quantities are selected as inputs by analyzing the model structure and calculating the correlation between the inertia time constant and other feature quantities. In addition, the computational results of traditional evaluation methods are incorporated into the data model inputs, and the model parameters are optimized using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The simulation results prove that the proposed method has certain advantages in improving the accuracy of inertia estimation compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: A Hybrid AC/DC Grid Optimal Dispatch Method Considering Total Transfer Capability Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid AC/DC grid dispatch method considering total transfer capability (TTC) constraints of transmission sections. A TTC calculation method combining optimal power flow (OPF) and repetitive power flow (RPF), OPF-RPF, is used to generate operational sample data. The samples are trained by the LightGBM (Light Gradient Boosting Machine) model. By solving the grid day-ahead optimization dispatch problem and conducting TTC verification iteratively, the dispatch plan that meets TTC constraints is finally obtained. Effectiveness of the method is validated on a hybrid AC/DC grid consisting of a 10-bus AC grid and a 4-bus flexible DC grid. Results show that the proposed method can ensure the secure and stable operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Clustering Algorithm Based User Group Structure Segmentation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Identifying high-value customers and providing quality services are essential for the transformation and advancement of power grid enterprises. This paper highlights the strategies necessary for achieving this transformation. Utilizing the load data collected by the measurement system of the power supply company, we analyze the load characteristics of users in typical industries through cluster analysis, a data mining technique. The hierarchical clustering algorithm can effectively extract the local characteristics of the data, determine the power supply mode according to the nature of users' electricity consumption, determine their electricity price strategy according to the types of electricity consumption, and dynamically adjust and implement the optimal service strategy according to the behavior of users.

articleTitle: Electric-Carbon Coordinated Scheduling of Community-Level Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the context of China's “Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality Goals”, integrating Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) with the power grid and distributed resources is crucial. VPPs help regulate electricity and carbon markets, addressing the instability of modern power systems. This study explores the regulatory roles of VPPs, trading strategies, and resource coordination, focusing on the synergy between electricity and carbon markets. First, the paper reviews current research on distributed resource scheduling, modeling, and electricity market bidding, highlighting the need for integration. It then proposes an integrated approach and analyzes global electricity markets, particularly the trends in new participants, auxiliary services, and clean energy consumption in China's market. Next, it outlines the trading framework for VPPs in electricity and auxiliary service markets and analyzes the carbon emissions trading (CET) market, laying the groundwork for carbon trading models. Finally, the study introduces a VPP “bidding + scheduling” decision-making model that integrates the electricity and CET markets. The model divides a day into 24 hourly nodes, using Monte Carlo scenario generation and probability distance elimination to forecast photovoltaic output. It aims to maximize VPP operator revenue in day-ahead electricity spot market trading, considering constraints such as interruptible loads, electric vehicles, gas turbines, and energy storage. A commercial complex case study validates the model's effectiveness by comparing scenarios with and without electricity-carbon coupling. This research offers insights into optimizing VPPs for sustainable development in the energy sector.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Dispatch Strategy for Virtual Power Plant Based on Bagging Ensemble Learning Forecasting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Virtual power plants (VPPs) struggle with peak-shaving due to unreliable distributed generation (DG) data and the intermittent nature of wind and solar power, impacting carbon emissions. This paper proposes a low-carbon dispatch strategy for VPPs based on a Bagging ensemble forecasting model. Firstly, a VPP dispatch framework based on DG output and load forecasting is established, and a Bagging ensemble forecasting model with feature selection is proposed. Secondly, the control characteristics of flexible industrial, commercial, and residential loads are analyzed to establish a control cost model, which is then integrated with the balanced relationship between wind, photovoltaic, and energy storage, as well as the carbon emission mechanism, to formulate a low-carbon dispatch model. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed strategy can improve the accuracy of DG output and load forecasting in complex feature environments while realizing the interaction between source-grid-load and reducing the generation and operation costs of the grid.

articleTitle: Credibility-Enhanced Blockchain for Distributed Security-Constrained Economic Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of distributed energy sources, it is highly important for power systems to reduce operation costs safely. Distributed security-constrained economic dispatch (SCED) methods are crucial to this end. Existing SCED methods cannot resist malicious attacks, and they have no warning or effective punishment for malicious parties. To bridge these gaps, this paper proposes a distributed SCED method based on blockchain with dual-factor punishment. The proposed method selects delegates from a coordination committee for information consensus to resist malicious attacks. The coordination committee members adjust their credibility scores at each iteration according to the behavior performance of the participants. The credibility score is employed to determine the punishment that the participant needs to be subjected to for SCED tasks. The numerical results verify the performance of the proposed method in terms of resisting malicious behaviors, warning and punishing malicious parties, and convergence.

articleTitle: On Security-Constrained Bidding of Shared Transportation Hubs for Renewable Fuels and Refined Oil Participating Within Energy, Regulation and Pipeline Logistics Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper investigates the security-constrained bidding strategy of the emerging shared transportation hubs for renewable fuels and refined oil (STH-RRs) participating within energy, regulation and pipeline logistics markets. Firstly, to excavate more flexible capability for the power system as well as to increase the revenue of the STH-RR operation company, the model for STH-RR participating in regulation market is established. Secondly, the security-constrained two-stage bidding model is first proposed for STH-RRs to balance the revenue across energy, regulation and pipeline logistics markets. Particularly, to guarantee secure operation of STH-RRs and meet the delivery demand, the rigorous multi-product transportation constraints are considered in both stages. Case studies based on the modified real-world multi-product pipelines in South China validate the proposed method, with the revenue and turnover increase of 14% and 4.7%, respectively, compared with conventional methods.

Author Keywords: Shared transportation hubs for renewable fuels and refined oil

articleTitle: An Improved ADP Algorithm for Multistage Unit Commitment of Renewable Energy Integrated Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the continuous penetration of renewable energy sources (RESs), the unit commitment (UC), as a key operational problem in power system, is facing increasingly challenges due to the uncertainties. This paper proposes a decomposed optimization algorithm for the multistage UC with the uncertainties of RESs. The Wasserstein metric-based distribution ally robust optimization (DRO) is extensively applied to handle the uncertainties in UC, and the UC is decomposed into a series of nested subproblems by improved approximate dynamic programming (ADP). Compared with traditional ADP algorithm, the proposed algorithm improves Lagrange cut-based value function to adaptively tackle integer variables, while provides tractable and favorable robust commitment strategies. Moreover, a parallel technique is further used to accelerate the algorithm in both scenario and stage levels. Case studies on several test systems illustrate that the proposed algorithm is favorable in terms of computational accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Advanced Methodology for Optimal Allocation of Reactive Voltage Control Utilizing Sensitivity Matrix Analysis and Distance Evaluation Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In practical power grid operations, dynamic reactive power sources, like the regulator, might struggle to supply ample dynamic reactive power support during fault-induced transients, especially when operating at near-capacity loads. Consequently, this research introduces a collaborative strategy designed to enhance the allocation of reactive power resources within the power system. This strategy ensures that the system maintains adequate dynamic reactive power reserves to address voltage fluctuations caused by faults during regular operation. Considering the reactive power equilibrium in power systems adheres to the “local balance” principle and exhibits characteristics of spatial and temporal interdependence, this paper suggests a novel reactive voltage control partitioning approach. This approach is grounded in the sensitivity matrix and a distance evaluation function, aiming to achieve spatial decoupling. The goal is to ensure that the system can promptly secure sufficient reactive power support in the event of a fault.

articleTitle: System Equivalent Inertia Evaluation Method Based on Steady-State Operational Data and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to accurately quantify the virtual inertia of wind turbines, a system equivalent inertia assessment method based on the steady-state operation data of a high percentage of new energy power systems is proposed. Firstly, the inertia composition of the new energy system is analyzed, the turbine virtual inertia and load inertia are fully considered, the equivalent inertia response model of the new energy system is established, and the actual inertia in the power system is calculated by using the conventional definition method. Then, the equivalent inertia assessment model based on a neural network is constructed based on the steady-state operation data of the power grid under different wind power penetration rates. At the same time, the model's training can be based entirely on historical steady-state operation data, which can realize the accurate assessment of system equivalent inertia without additional perturbation and improve the inertia assessment system.

articleTitle: A Spatial-Temporal Forecasting Method for Electric Vehicle Charging Load Based on GDC-LSTM User Travel Characteristics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this study, a spatio-temporal prediction model for EV charging loads is proposed based on the Graph diffusion convolution-Long short-term memory network (GDC-LSTM). This model integrates diverse sources of information, including weather conditions, day types, and temperatures. Firstly, the GDC-LSTM is employed to predict EV traffic flow data, capturing the travel patterns of EV users. Subsequently, a real-time model for EV power consumption is developed, and the floyd shortest path algorithm is optimized by introducing real-time road saturation data.. Finally, employing the Monte Carlo method, spatio-temporal distributions of various EV charging loads are forecasted and mapped onto distribution network nodes. The effectiveness of the methodology is verified by demonstrating the model's ability to predict EV travel behavior and load distribution through a case study in the main urban area of Chengdu, and evaluating the impact of load access on distribution network node voltages.

articleTitle: Operational Reliability Evaluation for Integrated Energy Systems Considering Demand Response and Time-Varying Component Failure Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: To improve the efficiency of operational reliability assessment and support risk prevention and control in system operation, this paper develops a demand response (DR) model based on tariff elasticity and load transfer rate to capture load changes before and after the implementation of time-of-day tariffs. An efficient model-data hybrid-driven approach is proposed for assessing the operational reliability of an integrated energy system taking into account the time-varying characteristics of component failure rates. Critical components are identified through risk factors based on price sensitivity and component operating conditions. A least squares support vector machine (LSSVM) is utilized to establish the relationship between reliability and load level for fast reliability updating. Case studies validate the computational efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dynamic Scheduling of Mobile Energy Storage for Post-Disaster Power Recovery from Storm Tides: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Storm tide disasters may lead to extensive power outage in distribution networks. The usage of energy storage resources is necessary to ensure the power critical loads. Previous research has been designed to address typhoon disasters without considering the impact of storm tides, which reduces its effectiveness. This paper proposes a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework to address the issues, based on the integration of power and transportation networks, facing dynamic scheduling decisions of mobile energy storage for power supply recovery after storm tide. Firstly, to simulate the dynamic allocation of power demand and energy storage resources in various regions during storm tide disasters, a coupled transportation and power grid digital twin is constructed, ensuring that Mobile Energy Storage Systems (MESS) can efficiently transfer and distribute power resources between regions affected by storm tide. Then, the reinforcement learning method based on Multi-Agent Depth Q-Network (MADQN) is designed, and can optimize the real-time scheduling strategy of mobile energy storage resources, maximize power recovery efficiency, and minimize recovery time. Finally, a hazard assessment framework for storm tides in coastal cities is proposed. The experimental results show that this method has significantly improved recovery speed and power supply security after storm-tide disasters.

articleTitle: Short-Term Multi-Energy Load Forecasting Based on Feature Reconstruction and TCN-Informer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: With the diversification of user energy and coordinated operation development of the integrated energy system, the coupling relationships between different energies becomes increasingly complex, which brings great challenges to short-term multi-energy load forecasting. Considering inadequate correlation analysis of influence factors and insufficient model learning ability to implicit coupling relationships, a short-term multi-energy load forecasting method is proposed based on feature reconstruction and TCN-informer. Firstly, the day-scale feature is screened and optimal feature sets are reconstructed via correlation analysis between load and influence factor time series in specific date. Secondly, combining TCN and informer network, the multi-energy load forecasting model is built via multi-task learning architecture. The input layer is composed of TCN, which can extract key information and temporal correlation of the input data. The shared layer is composed of Informer network, which can excavate inner relation between different loads effectively. Finally, simulation data sets generate from integrated energy system of the Tempe campus at Arizona State University. Prediction indicator comparison confirms effectiveness and superiority of feature reconstruction and TCN-informer multi-energy load forecasting model.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment of Energy-Transportation Coupled System with Unified Integration of Multi-Type Emergency Decisions Under Extreme Weather
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Modern urban infrastructure systems are interconnected. Under frequent extreme weather disasters, the interdependence between systems can lead to the spread of failures and risk-compounding effects. This paper proposes an operational model and assessment framework that can comprehensively consider various complex factors and fully assess the risk levels faced by urban infrastructure systems under extreme weather. First, using Monte Carlo simulation based on Latin hypercube sampling, this paper establishes a framework for simulating and quantifying the impact of extreme weather events on the coupled energy-transportation system. Then, considering the inherent differences between the energy and transportation systems, a unified power-heat-transportation emergency model is established, covering the entire process of prevention, response, and recovery. This model comprehensively accommodates various types of emergency decisions for the energy-transportation system in a unified form. Numerical experiments show that the proposed framework and model can reveal the risk levels faced by urban infrastructure systems, providing references for the handling of extreme weather events.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Storage Systems with Renewable Energy Generation and Consumption Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This work provides a comprehensive systematic review of optimization techniques using artificial intelligence (AI) for energy storage systems within renewable energy setups. The primary goals are to evaluate the latest technologies employed in forecasting models for renewable energy generation, load forecasting, and energy storage systems, alongside their construction parameters and optimization methods. The review highlights the progress achieved, identifies current challenges, and explores future research directions. Despite the extensive application of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) in renewable energy generation, consumption patterns, and storage optimization, few studies integrate these three aspects simultaneously, underscoring the significance of this work. The review encompasses studies from Web of Science, Scopus, and Science Direct up to December 2023, including works scheduled for publication in 2024. Each study related to renewable energy storage was individually analyzed to assess its objectives, methodology, and results. The findings reveal useful insights for developing AI models aimed at optimizing storage systems. However, critical areas need further exploration, such as real-time forecasting, long-term storage predictions, hybrid neural networks for demand-based generation forecasting, and the evaluation of various storage scales and battery technologies. The review also notes a significant gap in research on large-scale storage systems in Brazil and Latin America. In conclusion, the study emphasizes the need for continued research and the development of new algorithms to address existing limitations in the field.

articleTitle: Forecasting-Aided Voltage Estimation for Distribution Network Considering the Integrated Management of Virtual Power Plants Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As more distributed energy sources integrate into distribution networks, issues such as voltage fluctuations and reduced observability become increasingly prominent. Therefore, this paper proposes an algorithm for forecasting-aided state estimation (FASE) in virtual power plants' integrated operation management platform. Firstly, a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM)-Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithm for distribution network FASE is introduced. Secondly, the integrated management of virtual power plant platforms (IM-VPPP) enhances the observability of distribution networks. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, simulations are conducted using the IEEE 33-bus standard distribution system. Results demonstrate significant advantages of the algorithm in terms of accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Research on Energy Storage and Carbon Trading Scheduling Optimization of Integrated Energy System Considering Wind and Solar Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In response to the problem of low consumption rate caused by the volatility of renewable energy in the planning of electric gas thermal integrated energy systems, this article proposes an optimization method for energy storage carbon trading scheduling of integrated energy systems considering wind and solar consumption. Firstly, for the uncertainty of wind and solar power output fluctuations, a GAN network is used to generate a set of basic wind and solar scenes, and the scenes are compared and reduced to obtain typical wind and solar scenes; Secondly, a multi-objective optimization model is constructed with the lowest operating cost, optimal carbon emission reduction, and optimal wind and solar absorption rate; Finally, an optimization solution strategy for energy storage carbon trading scheduling is proposed, and a 14 node power grid, a 5-node gas grid, and a 3-node heating network are designed to plan and simulate the system. The simulation results show that the comprehensive energy system scheduling optimization model constructed in the article can ensure the wind and solar energy consumption rate while considering the system economy and meeting the low-carbon requirements of the comprehensive energy system.

articleTitle: Gas Pipeline Failure Detection Based on the Frequency-Domain Port Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In the integrated electricity and gas system (IEGS), a failure in the gas network may cause cascading failures in the power system, which requires the electric power control center (EPCC) to have a timely grasp of the gas failure information. In this paper, a gas pipeline failure detection model, including the leakage and the blockage failure, is proposed based on the frequency-domain port model (also known as the energy-circuit model), which only utilizes the pressure and flow measurements at the inlet and outlet of the pipeline. Firstly, the dynamic characteristic of the blockage and leakage of the pipeline is analyzed based on the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, which provides a practical way to simulate the dynamics of the gas pipeline failure. Secondly, the frequency-domain port model of the pipeline is constructed to estimate the pressure and flow series inside the pipeline based on the border measurements, the comparison of which indicates the failure information along the pipeline. Finally, a simple numerical example is designed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method where failure occurs in a single pipeline.

articleTitle: Electricity Spot Market Price Risk Assessment Considering the Participation of Various Aggregated Demand-Side Resources and the Impacts of Renewable Energy Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Owing to the volatility of renewable energy, primarily from wind and photovoltaic(PV) power, the incorporation of renewable energy installations can lead to fluctuations in electricity prices in the power market. The participation of various aggregated demand-side resources is an unavoidable trend in the electricity market's development, and the flexibility and adjustability of them can mitigate electricity price risks. In this paper, three types of aggregated resources, namely aggregators considering combined heat and power, energy storage aggregators, and load aggregators, are introduced. A method for assessing market price risk under the participation of various aggregated demand-side resources and the influence of fluctuations in renewable energy output is proposed. Firstly, an operating model for the three types of aggregated resources is established, and the output scenarios of renewable energy are generated using a normal distribution method. Secondly, a model for electricity market risk assessment is established, and the expected system electricity price is introduced as an evaluation index to quantify the electricity price risk in both cases, before and after the participation of aggregated resources. Finally, the suggested approach is confirmed through a modified IEEE 39-bus test system, with PV power serving as a representative example. The analysis results indicate that the introduction of aggregated resources can effectively mitigates the price risk attributed to the volatility of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Using Deep Reinforcement Learning in Optimal Energy Management for Residential House Aggregators with Uncertain User Behaviors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In this study, the home energy management problem, which can be regarded as a high-dimensional optimization problem, for numerous residential houses, is addressed. The concept of the aggregator is utilized to reduce the state and action space and to handle the high dimensionality. A two-stage deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based approach is proposed for the aggregators to track the schedule from a superior grid and guarantee the operation constraints. In the first stage, a DRL control agent is set to learn the optimal scheduling strategy interacting with the environment based on the soft-actor-critic framework and generate the aggregate control actions. In the second stage, the aggregate control actions are disaggregated to individual appliances considering the users' behaviors. The uncertainty of an electric vehicle's charging demand is quantitatively expressed based on the driver's experience. An aggregate anxiety concept is introduced to characterize the driver's anxiety on the electric vehicle's range and uncertain events. Finally, simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach under dynamic user behaviors, and comparisons show the superiority of the proposed approach over other benchmark methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of Data Quality Impact on Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Accurate load forecasting is essential for the stable operation and economic efficiency of power systems, particularly with the rise and renewable energy integration. However, the quality of load data plays a critical role in determining the accuracy of forecasting models. This paper explores the significant impact of data quality on load forecasting performance. Common issues such as missing values, outliers, and noise can distort historical load patterns, leading to suboptimal forecasts. To this end, this study examines the effects of data quality degradation on performance of various forecasting models, including traditional time-series models like ARIMA, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Specifically, we evaluate the performance of these models when trained on datasets with varying degrees of data corruption. Moreover, the study proposes methods for improving data quality, including imputation techniques for missing values, outlier detection and removal methods, and noise reduction strategies. Specifically, advanced imputation methods, such as K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and LSTM-based imputation, demonstrate superior performance in restoring data integrity compared to simpler methods like mean imputation. Finally, experimental results show the importance of ensuring high-quality data collection and processing in load forecasting.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power System Stability Under Slowly Varying Perturbations in Renewable Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: Although the impact of persistent perturbation from renewable energy on power system stability has been studied, the effects of slowly varying disturbances remain unexplored. This paper proposes a new stability concept, locally differential input-to-state stability (LDISS), based on the input-to-state stability framework. The new concept enables the characterization of system stability under slowly varying fluctuations in renewable energy output. A Lyapunov-like analysis method provides a stability condition for LDISS. The analytical approach is applied in a single-machine infinite-bus system with additive perturbation to analyze its stability. Experimental results on the same system verifies the theoretical method.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Time-sharing Tariff Policy on Regional Electricity Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: As an essential way of demand-side electric energy management, a time-sharing tariff policy changes the user's electricity consumption behavior through tariff signals, guides the user to participate in grid peaking, and adjusts the load peak-valley difference. Compared with the peak and valley tariff mechanism, it effectively strengthens new energy consumption and eases the grid trend back-feeding. It positively impacts power supply preservation, energy resource allocation, grid operation and other aspects. Based on the data of a city's power grid, this paper analyzes the influence of the TOU tariff policy on the power consumption in this region from the whole network load, power flow change and load forecast.

articleTitle: A Novel Diagonal-Laminated Fe-Based Nanocrystalline Ribbon Core Structure in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: In recent years, the application of nanocrystalline materials in wireless power transfer systems has been continuously investigated. However, due to their significantly higher conductivity characteristics than ferrite, they can trigger additional eddy current losses and attenuate the transmission efficiency of the system. This paper presents a novel diagonal-laminated Fe-based nanocrystalline magnetic structure, which significantly reduces the additional eddy current loss of typical flat-laminated nanocrystalline structures and possesses excellent shielding effects. The modeling and analytical calculations of magnetic shielding energy efficiency and eddy current losses are performed and discussed in conjunction with magnetic reluctance modeling and finite element simulations. The superiority of the proposed core structure is verified by comparative experiments with five different magnetic pads prototypes of WPT couplers. Results show that the shielding effect is almost comparable to that of the ferrite pads when transmitting 3 kW power. The system efficiency is higher than 93.4%. Specifically, compared with the ferrite pads, the proposed structure reduces the core weight and volume by about 15.6% and 32.5%, respectively, realizing the lightweight design and efficient operation of the system. The design and application of the proposed material and structure are not limited to the wireless power transfer technology field and may have some new inspirations for the design of motors, transformers, and inductors.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of District Cooling System With Thermal Energy Storage Based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: China has been rapidly expanding its wind and solar power generation capacity to support carbon neutrality in the power sector. However, the intermittent and unpredictable nature of these energy sources has made it harder to maintain a real-time supply-demand balance. One key strategy to address this is demand response, where flexible loads are adjusted to align with renewable energy generation through time-of-use or real-time pricing. Air conditioning, which can account for over 50% of peak summer electricity demand in some cities, is a prime target for demand response due to buildings' thermal inertia. This paper focuses on optimizing demand response control for large-scale district cooling systems under real-time pricing. We propose a reinforcement learning method based on a twin delayed policy gradient to optimize ice storage systems, managing uncertainties from both cooling demand and electricity prices. First, we model the problem as a Markov decision process, then adopt a model- free twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm to improve training efficiency and convergence. Simulation experiments validate the effectiveness of this control approach.

articleTitle: Game Theory Based Design of Flexibility Resource Utilization Mechanism for Integrated Electricity and Heat Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th Student Conference on Electric Machines and Systems (SCEMS)
abstract: This paper studies the cooperative game model of real-time flexibility resources in an integrated electric-thermal energy system. By shifting thermal loads, this model enables greater absorption of wind power, thereby improving the utilization efficiency of renewable energy. The cooperative game enhances the surplus of both the power grid and the thermal network through transfer payments, achieving a win-win situation. To further increase the willingness of the thermal network for flexible regulation, the paper proposes a method of compensating for long-term power changes, ensuring fair and reasonable distribution of benefits. Additionally, to ensure the safe operation of the thermal network, longer time-window safety constraints are introduced in the dispatch strategy, ensuring that the system remains safe and reliable during dynamic adjustments. The results of this study show that the proposed cooperative game mechanism significantly improves the real-time utilization efficiency of flexibility in the electric-thermal coupled system, increases system operation benefits, and ensures safe operation of the system.
